Deep scan needs the arp-scan package on the router. It broadcasts ARP requests across the subnet to find devices without a DHCP lease (for example ones with a static IP).

arp-scan is installed, but the router\'s rpcd only allows a few remote commands (ping, traceroute…) by default, so it needs a one-time grant.\n\nTap \"Copy Command\" and paste it into the router\'s SSH shell.

Run commands in plain language or directly
The terminal needs the luci-app-ttyd package.
ttyd usually listens on the LAN only. Make sure your phone is on the same network as the router.
ttyd requires a username and password that the app couldn\'t provide. Check the credential setting of ttyd in the web admin.
ttyd uses HTTPS with a certificate Android can\'t verify (usually self-signed). Turn off SSL for ttyd in the web admin and try again.
ttyd is bound to a UNIX socket and has no network port, so the app can\'t connect. Switch it to port mode in the web admin.
ttyd uses a random port (port=0), so the app can\'t connect. Set a fixed port in the web admin.
ttyd isn\'t running. Enable it under System → Terminal → Config in the web admin.

When on, you can describe what you want in plain language in AI Terminal; the AI suggests commands, runs them only after you confirm, and summarizes the results.\n\nUses DeepSeek with your own API key, billed per use. Each request sends your request, recent terminal output, and command results to DeepSeek. The key is stored encrypted on this device only.
Paste your DeepSeek API key (starts with sk-). You can create one at platform.deepseek.com.
AI Assistant is on. Tap the ✦ button at the top right of AI Terminal to use it.
Turning it off deletes the API key saved on this device.
Wake on LAN needs etherwake or wol on the router; installing luci-app-wol brings them in.
Sometimes only one of them works. If one fails, try the other.
The interface the magic packet is sent from, usually the LAN bridge (br-lan).
The target must have Wake-on-LAN enabled in its BIOS and network card, and be connected by Ethernet. The magic packet is one-way; the router gets no confirmation.
The router has neither etherwake nor wol. Install one from Package Manager.
A device that\'s powered off usually isn\'t in the list, so you can enter its MAC directly.
Invalid MAC address. It should be 12 hex digits, e.g. AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF.

Choose a host to wake first.
Magic packet sent to %1$s.\n\nThe target may take a few seconds to a minute to power on.

When on, commands from the AI run on your router right away, without asking you to confirm each one.

The AI can misunderstand you or suggest wrong commands, which could drop your network, lose settings, or lock you out of the router. High-risk commands (firewall, network interfaces, passwords, reboot, firmware, deleting files, etc.) still wait for your confirmation, but the risk level is judged by the AI and may be wrong.

You can tap Stop at any time while commands run. It turns off automatically when you leave AI Terminal.
⚡ High-risk commands don\'t run automatically. Review and run them yourself.
⚡ Ran automatically %1$d times in a row. Review before continuing.
